facts.fact: George Junor's nine (1913) and H. Chandler Egan's nine (1919), on a terrace above the Tualatin River.
A Pacific mastodon was found in Tualatin in 1962; its skeleton is shown in the Tualatin Public Library.

current.subject: An arched wooden footbridge over a creek.
current.weaknesses: Square scene with banks; the arch doesn't make a shape of its own.

concepts.name: The Moon Bridge
concepts.rationale: The arched bridge and its reflection close a circle on the water: a round emblem from the same subject.
concepts.symbolism: Crossing the river, a full circle.
concepts.tradeoffs: Moon bridges are a garden cliché.

concepts.name: The Tualatin Mastodon
concepts.rationale: An Ice Age mastodon walking across the card. Tualatin's best-known resident is 12,000 years older than its golf.
concepts.symbolism: Deep time and the town's own symbol.
concepts.strengths: Memorable and unique to the town.

recommendation: Concept 2. Nothing else in golf looks like it, and it is Tualatin's own story.
